episodes.title: Chandrayaan-2's Orbiter, Still at Work
sources: ISRO, Chandrayaan-2 mission page (isro.gov.in/Chandrayaan_2.html): 100 km lunar polar orbit; Vikram separated 2 September 2019; eight orbiter instruments; OHRC has the best resolution (0.3 m) of any lunar orbiter camera; expected life of about seven years against a planned one year

Wikipedia, 'Chandrayaan-2' (summary read): launched 22 July 2019 on LVM3-M1; Vikram crashed 6 September 2019 after a software glitch; the orbiter relayed for Chandrayaan-3; CLASS mapped sodium; CHACE-2 detected argon-40; chromium and manganese detected; XSM and CLASS observed a May 2024 solar flare

quiz.q: What did the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter do for Chandrayaan-3?
quiz.why: In 2023 the orbiter relayed communication for the Chandrayaan-3 lander.

quiz.q: Roughly how high above the Moon does the orbiter fly?
quiz.why: ISRO gives a 100 km lunar polar orbit.

quiz.q: Which Chandrayaan-2 instrument is the high-resolution camera?
quiz.why: OHRC, the Orbiter High Resolution Camera, resolves about 0.3 m.

review.note: Facts were read against ISRO's Chandrayaan-2 page; launch date, crash cause and science results come from the Wikipedia article and should be checked against ISRO before approval. The 'Relay' ring is decorative (full ring). Moving facts: the orbiter's remaining life and its science results keep changing.

episodes.title: Ballistic or Cruise: Two Kinds of Missile
sources: Wikipedia, 'Ballistic missile' (summary read): powered only for a short initial period, most of the flight unpowered; boost, mid-course and terminal phases; long-range (ICBM) trajectories peak well above 1,000 km, outside the atmosphere
Wikipedia, 'Cruise missile' (summary read): self-navigating, flies a non-ballistic, often very low path; aerodynamically guided in powered flight and stays within the atmosphere
PIB, 11 March 2024 (PRID 2013549): Mission Divyastra, the first flight test of Agni-5 with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle technology, from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha
DRDO, BrahMos page: BrahMos is a joint venture of DRDO (India) and NPOM (Russia); inducted into the Indian Navy and Army

quiz.q: For most of its flight, a ballistic missile is…
quiz.why: It burns only briefly at the start, then coasts along a ballistic path.

options: Agni-5 with multiple independently targetable warheads
quiz.why: PIB: the first flight test of Agni-5 with MIRV technology.

quiz.q: Which statement about cruise missiles is correct?
options: They stay in the atmosphere and are powered through flight
quiz.why: Cruise missiles fly like small planes, powered and within the air.

review.note: Physics of the two types comes from Wikipedia summaries; official confirmation is from PIB (Divyastra) and DRDO (BrahMos). No BrahMos speed is given because the figure was not read from an official page. The archive photo is from the SDASM negative collection; check it reads correctly (not an inverted negative) and that no logo shows. Only one picture was found under an allowed licence, so the video leans on diagrams. Moving facts: missile tests are frequent; check nothing newer changes the India card. The ICBM peak height was softened to 'more than a thousand kilometres', which every source agrees on.
